what: input: Chip description
value: A chip description lists core types (geometry, count, weight bits, sign granularity, bias, run-time writable matrix, write technology), the integer semantics and neuron model, the converter law at core outputs, the supported operation classes and banded cost constants

what: stage: Check
value: A deployment passing both is \emph{certified}: equal to $\iota$ for every input

what: output: Program
value: returns a program for the cores and the host CPU with its check

what: output: Verdict
value: or a refusal naming the stage and its reason

what: output: Verdict: outcome Bit-exact (the frozen text's name: Certified)
value: A deployment passing both is \emph{certified}: equal to $\iota$ for every input

what: output: Verdict: outcome Sample-checked (the frozen text's name: Sample-checked)
value: a deployment it does not establish is only \emph{built and checked}

what: output: Verdict: outcome Rejected (the frozen text's name: Refused by name)
value: else it is refused by name

what: output: Verdict: the printed outcome names (Bit-exact, Sample-checked, Rejected)
value: Passing both makes it \emph{bit-exact}: on the toolchain's model of the cores, with analog arrays idealized as exact, it equals its single-pass program for every input. This assumes a correct cut of the IR into core-sized tiles and correct code for that model and the single-pass program. Only the sampled run tests that code (Section~\ref{theory:sec:check}). Passing only the sampled run makes it \emph{built and checked}. A differing output yields a named refusal

what: output: Cost estimate
value: latency, energy, area and lifetime are estimates

what: loop: Exploration loop
value: the exploration adapts and checks a network once per setting of the properties that change the computation and visits each chip description at each core budget
